sentences.text: Mystiornis was approximately the size of a modern thrush.
The only known fossil of Mystiornis is an isolated metatarsus, a bone in the lower leg, found in the Shestakovo-1 locality in southern Western Siberia.
The genus Mystiornis was named in 2011 by Evgeny N. Kurochkin, Nikita V. Zelenkov, Alexandr O. Averianov, and Sergei V. Leshchinskiy.

Based on its shortened second metatarsal and the orientation of its trochleae, the pulley-like joints where tendons attach, Mystiornis possessed diving adaptations similar to those of Gansus and Neogaeornis.
Mystiornis belongs to the order Mystiornithiformes.
Mystiornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
